title: finger sequencer: six variations, one hand
steps: Open the finger sequencer on a drum track. (field steps: VERIFY)
Build a one-bar groove: kick, snare, hats. Keep it plain; it's the base every variation answers.
Put six variations of it on six white keys: fewer hats, a ghost kick on the a of 2, a late snare, a fill, a half-time feel, a drop with only hats. (field steps: VERIFY)
With Hold on, switch between the white keys one-handed while the loop runs, so the other hand is free to play. (field steps: VERIFY)
Arrange live: 4 bars of the base, 2 of a variation, back to the base, the fill on the last bar before a change.

title: endless sequencer: a 5-step motif
steps: Open the endless sequencer on a synth track. (field steps: VERIFY)
Enter a 5-step motif from the key's pentatonic: three notes and two rests. (field steps: VERIFY)
Let it run against the 4/4 loop. If each step is a 16th (field steps: VERIFY), the motif starts on a different 16th every bar and lines up with bar 1 again after 5 bars.
Move one rest one step and listen to how the accent shifts.

title: endless sequencer: a 6-step motif
steps: Open the endless sequencer on a synth track. (field steps: VERIFY)
Enter a 6-step motif: the chord's 3rd and 7th, a rest, the root, two rests. (field steps: VERIFY)
If each step is a 16th (field steps: VERIFY), 6 steps make a dotted-quarter figure: it lines up with the beat every 3 beats and with bar 1 every 3 bars.
When the chord changes, change only the 3rd and 7th steps to the new chord's guide tones.

title: endless sequencer: a 7-step motif
steps: Open the endless sequencer on a synth track. (field steps: VERIFY)
Enter a 7-step motif of four notes and three rests. (field steps: VERIFY)
Seven steps against a 16-step bar drift the most: use it for texture under a plain part, not as the lead.
Record 8 bars of it to tape unquantized (field steps: VERIFY), then play over the recording.

title: tombola: texture in the upper octave
steps: Open the tombola sequencer on a soft synth track. (field steps: VERIFY)
Feed it a few notes in the upper octave of the keyboard only, from the key's pentatonic. (field steps: VERIFY)
Keep its level low: it's texture behind the Push's chords, not a melody.
Let it run for 8 bars, then mute it on a section change. (field steps: VERIFY)
